paragraphs.zh: In certain embodiments, there is provided a process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) by oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) with an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst.
paragraphs.en: In certain embodiments, there is provided a process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) by oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) with an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst.
paragraphs.notes: Both spellings of the same moiety appear in this one paragraph, exactly as brief section 8 describes: 'methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA)' with a ph and 'methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST)' with an f, three lines apart. Transcribed as printed and not unified. The 2 of RuO2 is printed as a subscript; written here as a plain digit. Line number 5 sits in the left margin beside the last line of this paragraph and is not part of the text.

paragraphs.zh: According to embodiments of the present disclosure, the oxidant employed in the above reaction may be any oxidizing agent that can promote the target oxidation reaction. Examples of oxidizing agent include alkali metal hypochlorite and peroxide such as hydrogen peroxide.
paragraphs.en: According to embodiments of the present disclosure, the oxidant employed in the above reaction may be any oxidizing agent that can promote the target oxidation reaction. Examples of oxidizing agent include alkali metal hypochlorite and peroxide such as hydrogen peroxide.
paragraphs.notes: Line number 10 sits in the left margin beside the last line ('peroxide.') and is not part of the text.

paragraphs.zh: In certain embodiments, the ruthenium catalyst is oxidized by the hypochlorite to produce a mixture of ruthenate, perruthenate and ruthenium tetroxide. Preferably, oxidized to the ruthenate. At the end of the reaction, the ruthenium oxide is an insoluble solid present in substantially the same amount as initially so it can be filtered off and reused (for >50 conversion), even without treatment, in another cycle. The ruthenium can be supplied to the reaction solution in the form of a salt or an oxide, ruthenium dioxide and ruthenium dioxide hydrate. Preferably, in the form of ruthenium dioxide hydrate.
paragraphs.en: In certain embodiments, the ruthenium catalyst is oxidized by the hypochlorite to produce a mixture of ruthenate, perruthenate and ruthenium tetroxide. Preferably, oxidized to the ruthenate. At the end of the reaction, the ruthenium oxide is an insoluble solid present in substantially the same amount as initially so it can be filtered off and reused (for >50 conversion), even without treatment, in another cycle. The ruthenium can be supplied to the reaction solution in the form of a salt or an oxide, ruthenium dioxide and ruthenium dioxide hydrate. Preferably, in the form of ruthenium dioxide hydrate.
paragraphs.notes: Printing oddity kept as printed: '(for >50 conversion)' carries no percent sign after 50. Magnified at 3x to be sure; the line ends after '>50' and 'conversion)' opens the next line, and no percent glyph is inked on either. Do not repair it to 50%. Line number 15 sits in the left margin beside the line beginning 'conversion),' and is not part of the text.
